exposure: low rate of Assisted Vaginal Delivery (AVD)
outcome: increased neonatal mortality due to intrapartum asphyxia
increased maternal mortality due to a rise in second-stage caesarean deliveries
cohort: N/A - This is an expert opinion piece discussing birth outcomes generally in South Africa and high-income countries.
finding: A low rate of Assisted Vaginal Delivery (AVD) in South Africa is associated with increased neonatal morbidity and mortality and increased maternal morbidity and mortality due to a rise in second-stage caesarean deliveries.
mod_finding: The article's central argument is that failure to perform Assisted Vaginal Deliveries results in increased adverse outcomes for both neonates and mothers, highlighting the negative consequences of a shift towards second-stage caesarean deliveries.
